Maya: Heads-up — CI perf regression on next-token throughput after the allocator patch landed. Logs show spikes of OOM-like drops only for long-seq requests (seq>2048) in canary cluster.
Cheng: saw that metric too. perf-bot flagged a 12% p99 latency regression on g4dn-only canaries.
perf-bot: [CI] Regression detected: p99 latency +12% vs baseline on test-suite/long-seq (commit abcd1234).
Tom: quick dump from one failing pod: `OOM when allocating logits_slab size=1.2GB, free_pool_total=980MB, workspace_reserved=256MB`
Sasha: that suggests our workspace sizing + eager logits reuse policy is overcommitting for the kernel selected for long sequences. Kernel selector picked `attention_opt_v2` which increases intermediate activations.
Maya: right — kernel selector now prefers v2 for memory->compute tradeoff, but we didn't update the max_workspace heuristic. Result: logits slab tries to reuse large contiguous chunks and fails.
Cheng: can we reproduce locally? I ran `./perf_runner --model=gptx --seq=4096 --batch=2 --profile` and saw `alloc_fail` at token step ~512.
Tom: minimal repro snippet: ```bash
./perf_runner --model=gptx --seq=4096 --batch=2 --kernel=attention_opt_v2 --workspace_percent=0.2
```
Sasha: temporary mitigation: fallback kernel to `attention_v1` for seq>2048 in canary policy, that reduces memory but increases compute a bit. Want to push a canary patch?
Maya: propose a two-part fix: 1) make workspace sizing dynamic using 95th percentile sequence-length * batch from recent trace window; 2) conservative fallback for kernel selector when free_pool < threshold (e.g., 1.5x largest_logits_slab).
Cheng: +1. Also add a guard in allocator: if `alloc_request > free_pool_total - min_safety_guard`, try compact freelist / trigger async eviction instead of immediate OOM.
Tom: we should log detailed allocator decisions so we can trace why we chose reuse vs allocate. Suggest adding `allocator.debug_decision` events to traces with fields `decision, free_before, free_after_estimate, chosen_kernel` (simple string payload).
Sasha: agree. For canary rollout: patch kernel selector to prefer memory-slow path for seq>=2048, and enable dynamic workspace estimator set to 90th percentile for 24h window.
Maya: I'll open a small PR with the estimator (will default to old static percent). Will also add unit test for sequence extremes.
Cheng: I'll add the allocator guard + trace events. We'll run against the long-seq suite overnight.
Tom: FYI — embedding endpoint also hit a small regression related to KV cache sizing when using large prefix reuse; might be related to freelist fragmentation. Keeping an eye.
Maya: noted. After PRs, let's run both throughput and memory-stress harness. If green, canary with 5% traffic and extended monitoring for 48h.
Sasha: tx. For immediate action, I'm reverting the allocator patch in the canary branch to stop the regression while we iterate. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: [Action] Canary revert deployed (job #4827). Monitoring started.
Maya: thanks — will link PRs here once opened.
Cheng: also adding small perf test that runs sequence distribution sampled from production for more realistic workspace sizing in CI.
Maya: link to perf logs I uploaded: https://logs.internal/redwood/ci/1749998888/canary1 — includes `allocator.trace` + `kernel_choice` timelines.
Tom: good work. Postmortem note: need to ensure kernel selector and allocator invariants are co-evaluated during major runtime changes.
Sasha: agreed. Short RFC next week on joint kernel/allocator contracts.
Maya: filing RFC draft now.
Cheng: thanks all.
